source_snapshot.test_set: Intel CPU RAS -DRAM Parity Persistent Error
source_snapshot.procedure: Enable listed EDKII debug/WHEA controls, deploy Intel ITP, boot Windows, log and halt, run mc.dimminfo(), require CAP on, then issue literal `ei.injectCMDParityPersistent(socket, hbm=-1, mc, channel)` and resume.
source_snapshot.criteria: OS dmesg reports the matching error; BMC records a DIMM uncorrectable error without slot information; the front-panel fault light turns on; DIMM lightpath may turn on; optional UEFI records a DIMM uncorrectable error; Cscript reports successful CMD parity injection.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; delegates persistent parity injection to the user/FAE and proposes parity/persistent/uncorrected dmesg plus BMC SEL capture.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CHANGED; adds CAP/target validation, persistent-state clear/recovery, bounded injection, indicators and restoration.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly keeps the high-impact injector with the FAE, but its grep does not prove persistence, target, Cscript success, indicator behavior or safe clearing and assumes Linux dmesg on Windows.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly makes persistence clearing a mandatory recovery input, but repeats the source's non-runnable positional-after-keyword command.
historical_reviews.related_cases: The transient parity row expects a corrected event with indicators off and continued operation; this row expects uncorrectable persistent behavior, asserted fault indication and an explicit clear/recovery procedure.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Persistent fault state must have an approved clear path and must never be retried or cleared autonomously.

original_test_intent: Inject a persistent DRAM command/address parity fault into each approved memory-controller target with CAP enabled, verify uncorrectable persistent handling and Cscript success across OS/BMC/UEFI and physical indicators, then safely clear the state and recover the platform.
original_method: A qualified FAE/operator enables the approved debug/CAP settings, maps one socket/controller/channel target, supplies a vendor-valid persistent-parity call, performs one bounded injection, captures persistent status and uncorrectable evidence, observes fault indicators, executes the approved persistence-clear/recovery flow and restores configuration.
manual_activity: The operator/FAE must configure CAP/debug settings, provide the valid persistent-injection syntax, select the target, run one injection, observe indicators, clear the persistent state, recover and restore. The agent may not improvise any of these state-changing steps.
required_inputs: Socket/controller/channel/DIMM mapping and controller 1~N coverage matrix
Approved Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash, namespace and valid injectCMDParityPersistent signature
CAP semantics plus persistence lifetime and exact clear mechanism
Dedicated-SUT approval, backup, timeout, console recovery and BIOS restoration plan
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT with backup, stable power, independent console and qualified FAE
Preserve pre-state and existing logs; capture exact target and persistence-clear readiness before injection
Use only the approved syntactically valid persistent command and one target at a time
Stop on wrong target/severity, error storm, data-integrity concern, no-boot or inability to clear the persistent state
No automatic retry, reset or clearing; complete recovery and configuration restoration under the runbook
agent_execution_scope: Validate the supplied target/CAP captures and collect read-only Cscript, Windows, BMC, UEFI, indicator and recovery evidence
Do not repair syntax, select targets, change BIOS/CAP, inject, clear persistence, reset/retry or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve exact persistent Cscript interface and target coverage
Define CAP and persistence/clear semantics plus expected crash/recovery envelope
Specify BMC no-slot, optional UEFI, front-panel-on and DIMM-lightpath applicability

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The SSH grep cannot prove target identity, persistent state, injection success, indicator state or recovery; it conflicts with Windows and weakens SSH trust.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not execute `ei.injectCMDParityPersistent(socket, hbm=-1, mc, channel)`: its positional arguments after `hbm=-1` are syntactically invalid. Require the exact package-specific fully named call and clear sequence from the FAE.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CAP on, memory-controller 1~N, persistent parity intent and 20/20-minute estimates are retained; namespace, target and clear behavior are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Prove target and CAP pre-state, arm console and clear path, run exactly one approved persistent injection, correlate Cscript status with Windows/WHEA, BMC/UEFI and indicators, measure crash/recovery behavior, clear the persistent condition once and verify clean post-state/configuration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an executable interface and explicit persistence-clear lifecycle while preserving the intended fatal parity stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic uncorrected log neither proves persistence nor proves that the approved target, indicators and clear/recovery path behaved correctly.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Persistent parity state may cause repeated machine checks, crash loops, data loss or no-boot until vendor-specific clearing succeeds.

project_override_considerations: The persistent-state clear method is as critical as the injection itself. Its absence blocks execution but is not permission to downgrade the row to a transient test or claim DUT failure.
expected_evidence: Owner approval and full SUT/controller/DIMM/firmware/OS/BMC identity
Package version/hash, target coverage, BIOS/CAP pre/post state and armed recovery/clear path
Exact valid persistent command and complete Cscript success/output
Time-correlated Windows/WHEA persistent UCE, BMC uncorrectable no-slot event, applicable UEFI, front-panel-on and DIMM-lightpath evidence
Crash/recovery timing, persistence-clear transcript, clean health/restoration diff and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The literal persistent call is non-runnable because positional `mc, channel` follow keyword `hbm=-1`; controller 1~N lacks target coverage; Windows conflicts with dmesg; the Criteria says generic Cscript CMD parity rather than persistent success; and UEFI/DIMM-lightpath applicability plus persistence clearing are undefined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The persistent parity purpose and required recovery lifecycle are identifiable. Exact vendor syntax, target map, persistence oracle and clear path can be supplied by the FAE, so execution is conditionally gated rather than the review being irreducibly blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 21 Wistron-System RAS-00741-V003: provide the approved Intel ITP/CScripts version/hash, namespace and valid injectCMDParityPersistent signature replacing `ei.injectCMDParityPersistent(socket, hbm=-1, mc, channel)`; define CAP/persistence/clear semantics, controller 1~N target coverage, exact UCE/crash/recovery behavior, Cscript/Windows/BMC/UEFI/front-panel/DIMM-lightpath oracle and BIOS restoration.

review_improvement: This review prevents a malformed persistent-injection command and undefined clearing path from creating a crash loop or being mistaken for valid parity coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A persistent command/address parity error is not merely a higher-severity transient event: it can recur after resume and prevent normal boot until a vendor-specific state is cleared. The source command is syntactically invalid, so the precise package interface must be supplied rather than inferred. Evidence must demonstrate both that the intended controller produced the persistent UCE and that the approved clear/recovery operation returned the platform to a clean state. Because those inputs are obtainable from the FAE and the intent is otherwise clear, REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION remains appropriate instead of BLOCKED.
